sections.overview: Andersen’s small fruit-eating bat appears in this tree as Artibeus anderseni. The current ASM Mammal Diversity Database uses Dermanura anderseni, while some sources retain the broader genus Artibeus.
sections.identification: A Bolivian profile reports 8–12 g body mass, a stout skull under 20 mm basal length, and no third lower molar. It can resemble Dermanura cinerea; a Brazilian record warns of collection misidentifications.
sections.habitat: Its South American range covers Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, mainly at low elevations. Bolivian records include mature or young forest and forest islands; preference is unknown.
sections.diet: Diet records list mainly fruit and occasionally insects. The Bolivian conservation program reports that no local diet study is available.
sections.behavior: It builds leaf tents for daytime shelter; tent-making bats select characteristic leaf forms. Bolivian records include Heliconia, palm and banana leaves.
sections.reproduction: Pregnant females were recorded in Bolivia in July, September and October; these few records do not establish the full breeding season.
sections.ecology: By modifying leaves, it creates small sheltered roost structures within forest vegetation. Its fruit consumption links it to local plants, but its contribution to seed dispersal has not been measured.
sections.conservation: The latest IUCN assessment located, from 2016, rated it Least Concern; that assessment did not provide a population trend estimate.
